Insecurity Insight – Monitoring incidents around the world affecting aid, health care, education, and protection. 
 
. 
Attacks on Health Care 
News Brief 
10-23 June 
2026 
 
Since the adoption of United Nations Security Council Resolution 2286 in 2016 and 09 June 2026, Insecurity Insight has 
documented over 19,000 attacks on health care worldwide, highlighting the persistent and widespread failure to protect 
health care in conflict. 
To mark a decade since the adoption, Insecurity Insight released a landmark report analysing ten years of violence against 
health care. Drawing on a decade of systematically collected data, Still Under Attack documents the scale, patterns, and 
consequences of attacks on health care in conflict-affected settings around the world. Among the report's key findings: 
● More than 3,860 health workers were killed and over 2,500 were arrested or detained between January 2016 
and December 2025. 
● Local health workers remain particularly vulnerable, accounting for more than 65% of documented health worker 
killings. 
● The growing use of armed drones and explosive weapons is contributing to increasing damage to health facilities 
and to health worker deaths and injuries. 
 
Based exclusively on Insecurity Insight's data collection, the report shows how violence against health care has become 
increasingly normalised, with severe consequences for civilians, disease response, and the resilience of health systems. 
The report also provides detailed analysis of perpetrators, methods of attack, and emerging risks, including the growing 
role of new technologies in conflict. It concludes with recommendations for governments, international organisations, 
humanitarian actors, and the diplomatic community to strengthen the protection of health care and improve accountability 
for violations.
Insecurity Insight – Monitoring incidents around the world affecting aid, health care, education, and protection.

SHCC Attacks on Health Care 
The section aligns with the definition of attacks on health care used by the Safeguarding Health in 
Conflict Coalition (SHCC). 
Africa 
Democratic Republic of the Congo 
13 June 2026: In Watsa territory, Haut-Uele province, the head nurse at Mungbere General Referral 
Hospital was shot and killed by a soldier who was reportedly attempting to speak to a patient 
receiving treatment, and the nurse was shot while intervening to inquire about the situation and 
protect the patient. Source: Radio Okapi 
 
As reported on 14 June 2026: In Mongbwalu town, Djugu territory, Ituri province, health workers 
burying a suspected Ebola casualty were violently obstructed from accessing a coffin by residents. 
Police officers warned residents not to touch the coffin but were later forced to use warning shots 
and tear gas to allow health workers to retrieve the body. Source: Personal Communication 
 
15 June 2026: In Wanamahika Mutiri area, Butembo city, North Kivu province, Adventist 
(Wanamahika) Hospital was stormed by unidentified armed men carrying bladed weapons and 
knives, who abducted a woman and her six-year-old daughter from the facility. The child had tested 
positive for Ebola. The mother and daughter were later found at an Ebola treatment centre roughly 
18km from Butembo. Sources: Actualite, AOL, BBC and Reuters 
 
16 June 2026: In I turi province, five Ebola response workers were briefly kidnapped by armed 
groups. Sources: Namibia Daily News and United Nations 
 
16 June 2026: In Kakumba village, Walungu territory, South Kivu province, two Red Cross workers 
wearing Red Cross emblems were killed by armed men while on a mission to supervise drinking 
water supply work. The armed men allegedly knew the nature of their mission in the area. Sources: 
ICRC and Radio Okapi 
 
Insecurity Insight’s latest social media monitoring brief analyses public narratives surrounding the 17th Ebola epidemic 
in the Democratic Republic of the Congo between 15 June to 22 June 2026. Key findings: 
● Politics, not the outbreak, drove the conversation. Comment volume rose 33% on the previous period, but 
almost entirely on the back of a single statement by an opposition figure linking the DRC's World Cup 
performance to governance failures (1,160 comments, 26.5% of the total). Harmful content stayed minimal 
in posts and scattered in comments. 
● A government attempt to deflect criticism onto an NGO backfired. After a health organisation warned of 
"dangerous gaps" in the response, the government rejected the criticism as "alarmist" and urged NGOs to 
show restraint. The backlash was overwhelmingly h ostile to the government rather than the NGO, and 
dominated by the "Ebola business" corruption frame. 
● A cluster of attacks on Ebola facilities and health workers was amplified and reframed online. The incidents 
are real and corroborated, but their online life was driven by a small network of accounts - and the single 
highest-reach post had over 400,000 views. 
Read the brief in English and French. Visit our website for precious briefs.
Insecurity Insight – Monitoring incidents around the world affecting aid, health care, education, and protection. 
 
3 
Data from Insecurity Insight shows that since 21 May and 21 June 2026, at least 19 incidents of violence against or 
obstruction of health care impacting Ebola response measures were reported. Two Ebola treatment facilities were 
attacked and deliberately set on fire and another vandalised, damaging windows and a water supply system, 
compromising access to drinking water. Health workers were repeatedly assaulted, threatened and violently obstructed 
from performing their duties. 
 
Ethiopia 
13 June 2026: In Sir Iyasus kebele, Enemay woreda, East Gojjam zone, south -western Amhara 
region, a health facility was looted by ENDF members during a raid in the area. Source: Amhara 
Association of America 
 
Nigeria 
21 June 2026: In Kawel village, Mushere district, Bokkos local government area, Plateau state, a 
primary health centre was attacked by gunmen with guns and machetes at around 2330hrs, killing 
22 people, including an unspecified number of health workers and patients. Source: Daily Trust 
 
Sudan 
 
Data from Insecurity Insight shows that since fighting started between the SAF and RSF in April 2023 and 09 June 2026 
at least 761 incidents of violence against or obstruction of access to health care took place across Sudan: 
● Over two-thirds of these 761 attacks were attributed to the RSF 
● 211 health workers were killed, 15 kidnapped and 127 arrested 
● Health facilities were damaged 216 times 
● 63 attacks where armed drones affected health care 
● 51 attacks on maternal health care services

Asia 
Pakistan 
Between 05 June - 01 July 2026: In Quetta city, Balochistan province, a female doctor was attacked 
and severely burned with acid inside the Civil Hospital by a hospital lift operator. A medical technician 
was also burned when he rushed to help the doctor. The lift operator was later shot and killed by 
police who tracked him down at a local bus station. In response to the acid attack, doctors staged 
protests in Quetta. Sources: Arab News, Ians Live and The Jerusalem Post 
 
Myanmar 
 
 
Data collected by Insecurity Insight shows that since the military coup on 01 February 2021 and 04 June 2026 at least 
1,943 incidents of violence against or obstruction of access to health care took place across Myanmar: 
● equivalent to one attack on health care every day for more than five years 
● 65% of these attacks were attributed to the Myanmar Armed Forces (MAF) 
● 175 health workers were killed and 932 arrested 
● health facilities were damaged on at least 509 occasions 
So far this year, at least seven health workers were killed by explosive weapons. Five health workers were killed in 
three incidents involving MAF airstrikes: two occurred at prisoner -of-war detention facilities under the control of 
opposition forces in Ra khine and Yangon, while the third involved the bombing of a hospital located in areas under 
the control of the PDF in Sagaing. A further two health workers were killed in two separate roadside landmine

Europe 
Ukraine 
10 June 2026: In Industrialnyi district, Kharkiv city, raion and oblast, a private dental clinic and 
apartments were damaged when a Russian drone fell near a residential building, sparking a fire. 
Source: UA Varta 
 
11-12 June 2026: In Hlukhiv city and urban hromada, Shostka raion, Sumy oblast, a pharmacy and 
shops inside a shopping centre were damaged in an overnight drone attack by Russian forces. 
Source: Kordon Media 
 
13 June 2026: In Bilopillia city and urban hromada, Sumy raion and oblast, a 64-year-old nurse was 
killed after a Russian drone hit their car around 0730hrs. Her acquaintance who was driving was 
also injured. The nurse worked in the interventional radiology department of the Central City Clinical 
Hospital of the Sumy City Council. Sources: Central City Clinical Hospital, Kordon Media, Odin 
Doma Sumy and The Sumy Post 
 
15 June 2026 : In Kushugum rural settlement and settlement hromada, Zaporizhzhia raion and 
oblast, a parked ambulance was hit by a Russian drone strike on the territory of a medical facility. A 
female nurse was injured and the ambulance caught fire. Sources: InformZP, MIG, Regio News, 
State Emergency Service of Zaporizhzhia, The Head of Zaporizkaya OVA and UA Varta 
 
18 June 2026: In Pidserednie village, Prykolotne rural settlement, Kupiansk raion, Kharkiv oblast, 
an ambulance was damaged by Russian shelling. Source: UA Varta 
 
20 June 2026: In Nikopol raion, Dnipropetrovsk oblast, a pharmacy and other civilian infrastructure 
were damaged in a Russian attack on the oblast with artillery, missiles and drones. Sources: 057, 
Apostrophe, Censor, Dnepr Express, Dnipro Media, Dnipro News, DniproTV, DSNews, 
Hirchytsya, Interfax, Informator, Nikopolnews, Ukrainian Truth, Ukrinform and Vidomo 
 
Insecurity Insight has documented over 3,000 attacks on Ukraine’s health facilities, health workers and infrastructure 
since the start of Russia’s full -scale invasion on 24 February 2022 to 30 April 2026, averaging nearly two attacks per 
day. 
● Hospitals and clinics have been damaged or destroyed 1,632 times 
● 462 health workers have been killed and 476 others injured. 
● 113 attacks on services provided for women during pregnancy, childbirth and the postnatal period 
Explore this interactive map - a joint undertaking among Insecurity Insight, eyeWitness to Atrocities (eyeWitness), 
Media Initiative for Human Rights (MIHR), Physicians for Human Rights (PHR), Truth Hounds, and the Ukrainian 
Healthcare Center (UHC) - to see where incidents took place. Available in English and Ukrainian. Map filters include 
attacks on maternal and childcare services, military use of health facilities and attacks impacting energy and water 
supplies.

Insecurity Insight – Monitoring incidents around the world affecting aid, health care, education, and protection. 
 
5 
Middle East and North Africa 
Lebanon 
10 June 2026: In Haris municipality, Bint Jbeil district, South governorate, two Al-Risala Association 
paramedics were injured in an Israeli airstrike. Sources: Lebanese Ministry of Public and 26 
September 
 
10 June 2026: In Tyre city and district, South governorate, MSF temporarily suspended activities, 
including its mobile clinics and support to Jabal Amel Hospital, Qana Hospital and the Lebanese -
Italian Hospital, following large-scale evacuation orders issued by the Israeli army covering Tyre, its 
camps and several surrounding areas. MSF evacuated its teams to Sidon and stated that the 
suspension was due to the forced displacement of residents and the deteriorating security situation. 
Source: Syrian Arab News Agency 
 
11 June 2026: In Tyre district, South governorate, the vicinity of Hiram Hospital was hit by an Israeli 
airstrike, injuring 10 nurses and hospital staff members. Patient rooms and the emergency 
department were damaged, and windows were shattered in staff vehicles. Sources: Drop Site and 
UN News 
 
21 June 2026: In Sidon city, Tyre district, South governorate, a pregnant nurse was killed in an 
Israeli airstrike. Source: Quds News Network 
 
Occupied Palestinian territory 
 
Data collected by Insecurity Insight shows that between 07 October 2023 and 09 June 2026, at least 3,327 incidents of 
violence against or obstruction of access to health care took place across the occupied Palestinian territory.1 95% of all 
incidents were attributed to Israeli forces. 
● Gaza: 2,328 attacks on health care were recorded during which health facilities were damaged 448 times, 765 
health workers were killed and 398 arrested.2 Patient access to medicine was obstructed on 289 occasions. 
● West Bank and East Jerusalem: 938 attacks on health care were recorded during which health facilities were 
damaged 30 times, 12 health workers were killed and 188 arrested. Patient access to medicine was obstructed 
on 579 occasions. 
Of the 938 attacks on health care in the West Bank, 47 were attributed to Israeli settlers, who were typically armed with 
guns or rocks. The proportion of such attacks more than doubled in 2025 compared to 2024, rising from around 2% to 
9% of total reported attacks. Between 01 January and 09 June 2026, Israeli settler-attributed attacks increased further, 
accounting for 22% of all reported attacks during that period. Most Israeli settler attacks on health care targeted 
ambulances and first responders, including blocking their access to those needing care. On at least seven occasions, 
Israeli settlers attacked health care under the protection of the IDF. 
Incident briefs: 10-23 June; 27 May-09 June; 13-26 May; 29 April-12 May; 15-28 April; 01-14 April; 18-31 March; 04-
17 March; 18 February-03 March; 04-17 February; 21 January-03 February; 07-20 January; All 
 
SHCC Factsheets (EN): 2025; 2024; 2023; 2022; 2021. (AR): 2025; 2024; 2023; 2022; 2021. 
 
Syrian Arab Republic 
As reported on 15 June 2026: In Ar Raqqa city and governorate, the vicinity of the National Hospital 
and Intifada School was under threat when the Interior Ministry was attacked in a suicide bombing 
by unidentified perpetrators, killing two employees of the Interior Ministry. One of the attackers was 
killed by intervening security forces, while the other was killed in the detonation. Source: Al Bilad 
Press 
 
Yemen 
11 June 2026: In Al-Darain area, Sheikh Othman district, Aden city, two doctors who were husband 
and wife, both employed at Doctors' Tower Hospital, were shot and killed alongside two Yemeni

6 
soldiers, and an unspecified number of others were wounded, when a soldier guarding the home of 
the governor of Yemen opened fire in the morning. The soldier was later killed during an attempted 
arrest by security forces. Sources: Al Bilad, Al Montasaf, The Independent and Yemen Shabab 
The Americas 
Colombia 
18 June 2026: In García Herreros neighbourhood, Cúcuta city, Norte de Santander department, a 
pharmacy was robbed and an employee threatened and hit by two men armed with pistols. Cash 
was stolen from the register. Source: Cucuta Online 
 
Haiti 
18-19 April 2026: In Port-au-Prince city and arrondissement, MSF staff members were trapped in 
their homes during clashes between rival armed groups with intense gunfire. Nearly 40 people, 
including the MSF staff and their families, sought refuge in the MSF hospital in Cité Soleil, having no 
other safe option. Source: MSF 
 
15 June 2026 : In Cité Soleil, Port -au-Prince city and arrondissement, the MSF -supported Isaïe 
Jeanty Maternity Hospital was hit and damaged by numerous stray bullets amid crossfire between 
armed groups. A woman was injured in the leg by a stray bullet inside the hospita l grounds. MSF 
suspended activities the next morning but continued to provide emergency care, patients’ 
stabilisation and referrals for several days. On 19 June, the organisation evacuated its staff and 
suspended all activities. Source: MSF
Insecurity Insight – Monitoring incidents around the world affecting aid, health care, education, and protection. 
 
7 
 
 
Other resources 
Attacks on health care were relentless in 2025. Using data collected by Insecurity Insight, the Safeguarding Health in 
Conflict Coalition (SHCC) recorded 2,546 incidents in 33 countries in which damage to or the destruction of health 
care facilities was reported on at least 790 occasions, 455 health workers were killed, 218 kidnapped and 263 arrested. 
Key findings in 2025 
● Violence rose in 13 countries and recorded incidents remained far above the ten-
year annual average. 
● Continued high levels of violence by state forces alongside rising levels of violence 
by non-state armed actors. 
● The expansion of remotely piloted aerial systems (drones) increasingly affected 
health care in conflict settings. 
● Kidnapping of health workers increased, particularly in the Central African 
Republic, Colombia, the DRC, Mali, Pakistan and Syria. 
The report includes detailed profiles of 21 countries and territories where many acts of 
violence against health care by state parties and non -state armed groups, including 
organized criminal groups, took place. These include: 
Africa: Burkina Faso, Cameroon, the CAR, the DRC, Ethiopia, Mali, Nigeria, Somalia, South Sudan and Sudan 
Asia: Myanmar and Pakistan 
The Middle East and Europe: Lebanon, Iran, the occupied Palestinian territory; Syria, Ukraine and Yemen 
The Americas: Colombia, Haiti and Mexico 
Year in Review: 2025; 2024; 2023 
 
 
Global Health Conference: The Right to Health in Times of War 
Bringing together health professionals, researchers, and activists, the conference will examine why medical neutrality 
is being eroded, what this means for affected populations in and beyond the immediate line of fire, and how health can 
be protected under conditions of violence. 
The program includes a keynote by Christina Wille (Insecurity Insight/Safeguarding Health in Conflict Coalition) as 
well as workshops with experts from Sudan, Lebanon, and Ukraine, including Hind Altaif (Emergency Response 
Rooms Sudan) and Dr. Zeina Mohanna (Amel Association International, Lebanon). The conference will address health 
systems under strain beyond active conflict zones, focusing on the militarisation and gradual erosion of health care as 
well as the ethical implications of these developments. Contributors include Prof. Dr. Yudit Namer (University of 
Twente) and the Gesundheitskollektiv Berlin. 
Date: 12 September 2026, 0930-1700 CET 
Location: Refugio Berlin 
Register here. Space is limited - we encourage you to secure your spot early. 
 
This Bi-Monthly News Brief comprises threats and violence as well as protests and other events affecting the delivery of and 
access to health care. It is part of the Attacks on Health Care project by Insecurity Insight. It is prepared from information available in 
local, national and international news outlets and online databases. The incidents reported are not a complete nor a representative list 
of all events that affected the provision of health care and hav e not been independently verified. All decisio ns made, on the basis of, 
or with consideration to, such information remains the responsibility of their respective organisations. Please get in touch if you are 
interested in curated datasets, if you have made a public statement that you would like us to include in our Bi Monthly News Brief, to 
report an incident or if you have additional information on an incident we have reported on. Join our mailing list.

Accordingly, our respective Governments, through representatives assembled in the city of San Francisco, who have exhibited their full powers found to be in good and due form, have agreed to the present Charter of the United Nations and do hereby establish an international organization to be known as the United Nations.
